correctness.rationale: For each fixed real α>−1, the stated monomial normalization and angular orthogonality reduce the eigenvalues of the bounded Toeplitz operator to the beta-normalized scalar integral. Take s=1−t and ζ=exp(−iπ/4). On the tiny lower-sector arc, |exp(i/s)|≤1 and the arc integral is O(ε^(α+1)); the bridge from ζ to 1 has |1−s|≤|1−ζ|<1. On s=ζu/√n, the leading exponential is exp(−ζ√n(u+1/u)), since i/ζ=−ζ; the subleading analytic factor at u=1 is exp(−ζ²/2)=exp(i/2). Along the ray |1−ζr|²=1−√2 r+r² for 0≤r≤1, giving a uniform exponential tail bound for large u; the reciprocal term bounds small u. On a compact interval away from the minimum u=1 there is a strict real-part gap. On u=1+n^(−1/4)v, the exact identity u+1/u−2=(u−1)^2/u gives Gaussian localization. For example, in the symmetric window |v|≤n^(1/20) the order n^(−1/4) correction is an odd linear-plus-cubic term and integrates to zero; Taylor's remaining integrand is bounded by n^(−1/2) times a fixed polynomial against a decaying Gaussian, while the rest of the neighborhood is negligible. The integral is thus asymptotic to √π ζ^(α+1/2) exp(i/2) n^(−α/2−3/4) exp(−2ζ√n) with the stated relative error. Dividing by Γ(α+1)n^(−α−1)(1+O_α(n^−1)) gives the exact constant, power and phase. The nonzero leading term gives the logarithmic limit, and diagonal singular values are the moduli, giving every Schatten class. The independent Kummer-function reduction in the originality evidence checks the same constants and error. The supplied quadrature source was inspected, not executed; its reported 12 ratio checks and four decay checks are corroboration only.

evidence: At a=n+1, b=−α, z=−i, the leading term of 13.8.11 and 10.40.2 is U(a,−α,−i)=√π exp(−i/2)(−i)^(α/2+1/4) a^(−α/2−3/4) exp(−2√(−ia))/Γ(a)·(1+O_α(a^−1/2)).
